newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan unions cool on long-term labor peace.
newsitem.headline: Alcan unions cool on long-term labor peace.

text.p: Unionized workers at Alcan Aluminium Ltd's Arvida, Quebec complex are not prepared to negotiate a long-term labor contract that would meet Alcan's request for labor peace until 2015, union officials said.

Officials with the Syndicat National des Employes de l'Aluminium d'Arvida (SNEAA), which represents 3,500 employees at Alcan's Arvida works, told members at a meeting on Tuesday night that the union would only discuss the company's proposal again after summer vacations.

"In effect, the plan tabled by Alcan proposes to protect operations by avoiding work stoppages caused by strike or lockout in exchange for job security," union president Jean-Marc Crevier told members.
Crevier said strikes remained the only way the union could make the company "understand reason," so union members would need to examine Alcan's proposal very carefully.
An 11-day strike by Alcan's Quebec smelter workers in 1995 cost the company US$70 million.
Alcan is mulling a C$1.5 billion smelter investment in Quebec and has said labor stability would be a prerequisite.
